body:
alex: noticing a weird p50 jitter on short requests this morning, looked like a regression after yesterday's kernel selector tweak :thinking:

rachel: same, saw a spike around 08:13 UTC on the canary pool. p50 went from ~18ms to ~45ms for seq<=32 workloads.

devon: do we have a repro? continuous batching + kernel switch maybe?

alex: yes, repro on an A100 instance with workload replay. If continuous batching groups a long seq before a short seq, kernel selector flips to the long-path kernel and launch overhead for the short path increases. KV warmup also shows extra misses.

lena: can you paste the sampling traces / pprof?

alex: attach below (abridged):
```
# top of pprof - alloc_space
0.42s  35.1% 35.1%  runtime.startSchedule
0.18s  15.0% 50.1%  kernel_selector.choose_path
0.12s  10.0% 60.1%  launch_manager.launch_kernel_async
0.10s   8.3% 68.4%  kv_cache.populate
```

rachel: kernel_selector.choose_path is surprisingly high for short seq traces. Is autotune re-evaluating too eagerly?

devon: autotune is checking seq-length histograms every N requests (N=50). If batch composition is bursty the selector can flip mid-stream. That flip causes a different kernel codepath and we pay a cold-launch penalty.

alex: noted that when kernel flips we also lose KV cache locality because different kernel variants use slightly different key indexing layout (small mismatch). kv_cache.populate has more time on flipped traces.

lena: hmm that index layout divergence is bad. Is that intended? I thought variants shared the same KV layout.

devon: historically they did, but an optimization for the wide-attn kernel added a prepacked index to reduce memory indirections. It wasn't guarded in selector invariants.

rachel: mitigation idea: add a hysteresis window for selector flips and prefer currently-warmed kernel if the expected launch cost > threshold. Also tighten KV invariants so kernels share layout or add fast copy path.

alex: tried a quick patch: keep current kernel pinned for 200ms after a flip unless 90% of samples indicate strong shift. Local replay shows p50 back to 20ms.

devon: nice. Any regressions for long sequences?

alex: minimal on our replay set. The overhead is only on short seq skew bursts.

lena: let's also add a metric: kernel_flip_rate per model+instance and kv_miss_rate at kernel-change. We can alert when flip_rate>0.05 and kv_miss spikes.

perfbot: automated test ran: replay suite after alex patch -> p50 delta -14ms on short seq, no regressed tail >1%. :white_check_mark:

rachel: can we get a canary rollout? maybe 10% of traffic pinned to the patched selector with a fallback to previous behavior.

devon: will create a canary via rollout config. plan: 10% for 2h, monitor kernel_flip_rate, p50, kv_miss. rollback if p50 > baseline +5ms or kv_miss > baseline*1.5.

alex: also adding unit test for kv layout compatibility check in the kernel registration path.

lena: thanks. follow-up owners: devon rollout, alex selector + tests, rachel metrics + dashboards.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: selector-hysteresis v2 -> canary pool (10%) by devon. ETA 6m. :rocket: 

rachel: great. if the canary looks good we'll promote and schedule a cleanup for the prepacked-index change (either revert or make layout-compatible).

alex: FYI the replay script used:
```bash
./replay.sh --model gpt-small --seq-dist short-heavy --host localhost:8080 --samples 5000
```

devon: thx — will watch metrics and post a short summary after 2h. :eyes:

rachel: thanks team, big win if hysteresis holds.

alex: one more note — we should document kernel selection invariants in the runtime README so future kernel authors don't accidentally change KV indexing assumptions.

lena: agreed, adding a doc ticket. :+1:

devon: summary posted in #eng-runtime after canary window.
